items.title: Culinary Knowledge and Skills Performance Among Grade 9 Learners: Basis for Curricular Intervention
items.abstract: Abstract. This study assessed Grade 9 students' culinary knowledge and skills performance at Cookery Agong-ong National High School in Butuan City to inform curricular intervention. Specifically, it examined students' engagement in Cookery in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and safety; assessed their food preparation and plating performance; determined the relationship between student engagement and performance in culinary knowledge and skills; and developed a proposed curricular intervention. The study employed a descriptive-correlational research design. Data were gathered through a structured knowledge test and a performance-based assessment tool anchored on competency standards adapted from TESDA's Cookery NC II framework. The study used percentages, means, standard deviations, and Spearman's rank-order correlation to analyze the data. The findings showed high self-reported student engagement in accuracy (M = 3.82), safety and sanitation (M = 3.77), and efficiency (M = 3.70). Learners also demonstrated excellent performance in preparing tools, equipment, and ingredients (M = 3.79), applying cooking methods and techniques (M = 3.72), kitchen safety and sanitation (M = 3.77), food presentation and plating (M = 3.79), and food storage and packaging (M = 3.68). The study also found a strong, statistically significant positive relationship between student engagement and performance in culinary knowledge and skills (\(\rho = .976, p < .001\)). Based on these findings, the study proposed a Cookery Competency Enhancement Program emphasizing hands-on, competency-based, collaborative, and performance-oriented activities targeting food storage temperature, occupational health and safety, ingredient quality, cooking adaptability, and food presentation. Keywords: Competency Enhancement, Cookery, Culinary Knowledge, Curricular Intervention, Skills Performance, Student Engagement

items.title: Decision Time Constraints and Trust Propagation in Multi-Operator Multi-Autonomy Teaming
items.abstract: Modern human–autonomy teams (HATs) often operate under time constraints that limit individuals’ ability to fully evaluate recommendations from the automation and autonomous systems. In these settings, people may rely not only on their own interactions with autonomy, but also on cues from their teammates. This study examines how decision time constraints influence trust propagation in multi-operator, multi-autonomy (MOMA) teams. Participants worked in pairs with two drones in a repeated threat-detection task, making rapid decisions under either standard (3.0 s) or constrained (1.7 s) time conditions. After each round, participants reported their trust in both drones and their teammate, allowing us to quantify how trust propagates based on teammate-reported trust. Results show that trust propagates between teammates in both conditions ( p < . 001), with stronger effects under tighter time constraints (3.0 s: b = 0.29; 1.7 s: b = 0.35). These findings highlight the role of social influences on trust in time-constrained environments and inform the design of human–autonomy systems for high-tempo operations.

items.title: Designing Chatbots for Person-Centered Care: Insights from Contraceptive Care in Kenyan Pharmacies
items.abstract: Adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) in sub-Saharan Africa face barriers to contraceptive access and lack decision-support resources tailored to their needs. Many Kenyan AGYW seek contraceptive services in the pharmacy setting, but experience stigma, judgment, and privacy concerns that make it difficult to seek guidance from pharmacists. This work examines how chatbots could integrate into Kenya’s pharmacy setting to support AGYW’s contraceptive decision-making. We presented chatbot prototypes in co-design workshops with AGYW and pharmacy workers to evoke reflections on perceived opportunities, concerns, and preferable futures of chatbot-supported care. Our findings highlight expectations that a chatbot could offer private, non-judgmental spaces for information seeking while shifting trust and authority away from pharmacists, revealing tensions surrounding the distribution of authority, reliance, and control among AGYW, pharmacists, and the chatbot. In response to these tensions, we contribute design guidelines for chatbots to navigate community beliefs and promote shared decision-making by AGYW and pharmacists. More broadly, this work extends research on sensitive health chatbots for youth by showing how such tools embedded within a service delivery setting surface distinct considerations for stakeholder roles and person-centered care.

items.title: DESIGNING COLLABORATIVE ROBOTICS FOR AUTOMOTIVE DEFECT DETECTION AND REPAIR: A HUMAN-CENTERED APPROACH
items.abstract: The increasing deployment of collaborative robots (cobots) in industrial settings requires a nuanced understanding of their impact on workers.Unlike traditional automation that replaces human tasks, cobots are designed to complement and enhance human capabilities.This study reports a human-centered investigation within the MAGICIAN project, which develops cobot-supported defect detection and repair for automotive manufacturing.Fieldwork at Tofaş in Türkiye combined structured observations of eight workers across Bodyshop and Press settings, 31 stakeholder interviews, and unweighted NASA-TLX assessments with 27 workers.We detail how observational records, stakeholder accounts, and workload patterns were triangulated and translated into traceable requirements.Results identify high temporal and effort demands, distinct workload profiles between production areas, reliance on tacit visual and tactile expertise, and the importance of predictability, worker control, and integration with existing reporting practices.This work contributes to an empirically grounded requirements-elicitation framework, and a transparent, confidence-aware cobot architecture that preserves human oversight while reducing repetitive physical and cognitive strain.

items.title: Designing Critical Human–AI Learning in Higher Education: The SC-AIM–FAVIC Framework for Analytical and Logical Reasoning
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is now routine in university study, yet unstructured use risks cognitive offloading, surface learning, and uncritical acceptance of fluent but unreliable output. This article aimed to develop and specify the Symbiotic Critical Human–AI Learning Model (SC-AIM), operationalised through the five-stage FAVIC framework (Formulation, Augmentation, Verification, Integration, Creation), and to set out the assessment instruments and evaluation design that accompany it. Following the Analysis and Design phases of the ADDIE research-and-development approach, we synthesised recent experimental, meta-analytic, and survey evidence to derive design requirements, translated them into a stage-by-stage instructional specification, built a process-sensitive assessment rubric, and defined a quasi-experimental and qualitative validation plan for Indonesian higher education. The results are the model and its components: an evidence-to-design mapping, the FAVIC stage specification, a three-level process-sensitive rubric, and an evaluation design with hypotheses. Conclusion: SC-AIM offers lecturers a concrete, theory-grounded sequence that places human reasoning before and after AI assistance and makes verification an assessed activity, giving higher education a ready-to-use pedagogical model for developing analytical and logical reasoning in the age of generative AI.

items.title: Development and validation of a scale assessing perceived trustworthiness in large language models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly part of everyday life, yet there is no established way to measure how users evaluate their trustworthiness. This study introduces the Perceived Trustworthiness of LLMs scale (PT-LLM-8), a self-report psychometric instrument measuring users’ perceived trustworthiness of their primary LLM. PT-LLM-8 is developed from the TrustLLM framework and adapted as a human-centred measure. The PT-LLM-8 comprises eight items representing truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, transparency, accountability, and compliance with laws. Psychometric properties of the scale were tested with 752 LLM users in the United Kingdom (Mean age = 28.58, SD = 6.11, 50.3% males, 48.8% females). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a one-factor structure, with high internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.90, Composite Reliability = 0.91, strong item-total correlations (ranged between 0.62 and 0.75), and measurement invariance across gender. The total score measures overall perceived trustworthiness, while individual item responses may also be examined descriptively for information about the content represented by each item. For researchers, practitioners, and developers, the PT-LLM-8 offers a practical instrument for evaluating interventions, comparing groups and contexts, and examining whether technical safeguards are reflected in users’ perceived trustworthiness of LLM. The scale can also be applied to guide system design, support policy development, and help organisations monitor shifts in user trust toward LLMs over time, making it applicable across research, practice, and governance.

items.title: Do what you want to do: an analysis of positive mental health literacy among pre-service teachers at a regional university in China
items.abstract: Positive mental health literacy (PMHL) is an important resource for promoting psychological wellbeing and resilience. Research on teachers’ mental health literacy has, however, concentrated on the recognition of mental illness among in-service teachers; its positive dimension has rarely been examined among pre-service teachers, and never in relation to their motivation for entering the profession. This study investigated the level of PMHL among pre-service teachers, examined differences in PMHL across demographic and background characteristics, and explored their perceptions of factors related to positive mental health. A convergent mixed-methods design was adopted, and data were collected from 455 pre-service teachers at a regional teacher-education university in Hunan Province, China, using a questionnaire comprising demographic items, a PMHL scale, and four open-ended questions. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t -tests, and one-way ANOVA, while qualitative data were analysed through thematic analysis. The findings showed that pre-service teachers demonstrated a generally high level of PMHL ( M = 3.78, SD = 0.67). Statistically significant differences were found according to year of study, gender and career motivation, and career motivation was associated with the largest effect (η 2 = 0.086), followed by year of study (η 2 = 0.029) and gender ( d = −0.34). A small difference by major (η 2 = 0.024, p = 0.049) did not survive correction for multiple comparisons and is reported as tentative. No significant differences were observed for admission pathway, age, family background, or teaching practicum experience. Qualitative findings revealed that employment and future competition pressure were the most frequently reported sources of stress, whereas leisure activities, social support, personal goals, and life adjustment were commonly identified as factors supporting positive mental health. Because the design is cross-sectional, these results describe associations rather than causal pathways, and they characterize pre-service teachers at one regional university rather than in China as a whole. Within these limits, the findings highlight the importance of strengthening pre-service teachers’ intrinsic motivation for teaching, so that their learning is driven more by interest, purpose, and positive psychological engagement.

items.title: Earthquake early warning as a socio-technical system: a cross-country systematic literature review
items.abstract: Earthquake Early Warning systems have expanded, yet their effectiveness depends on technical performance and whether warnings prompt timely protective action. This systematic review examines interactions among technical, institutional, and behavioural dimensions across EEW contexts. Following PRISMA 2020, literature published between 1975 and August 2026 was searched using Scopus and Massey University Library Discover. Of 1,202 records, 62 studies met the inclusion criteria. Evidence was synthesised across eight jurisdictions: Japan, Mexico, Taiwan, the United States, Aotearoa New Zealand, Switzerland, China, and Israel. Comparisons considered system maturity, technical architecture, public exposure, and differences among retrospective reports of alert responses, experiment, and stated intentions. EEW was generally perceived as valuable for situational awareness and psychological preparedness, but immediate protective action remained inconsistent. System maturity, alert thresholds, governance, risk communication, public knowledge, and preparedness practices were associated with variation in the warning-to-action pathway. Familiarity with established systems did not necessarily translate into protective action, highlighting the importance of context-specific guidance, institutional clarity, preparedness training, and accessible communication. The findings frame EEW as a socio-technical system in which technical capability creates the opportunity for protective action, while institutional, social, and behavioural conditions influence how that opportunity is used and may contribute to risk reduction.

items.title: Educação na sociedade do excesso de informação: da abundância de dados à formação do julgamento crítico
items.abstract: Este artigo analisa o significado de educar em uma sociedade caracterizada pela abundância, pela velocidade e pela competição entre fontes de informação. Parte-se do problema de que ampliar o acesso a conteúdos não equivale a ampliar conhecimento, compreensão ou capacidade de julgamento. O objetivo é discutir como as instituições educacionais podem articular repertório de conhecimentos, alfabetização midiática e informacional, avaliação de fontes, raciocínio sobre evidências e uso responsável de tecnologias digitais para formar sujeitos capazes de decidir em ambientes de incerteza informacional. Metodologicamente, desenvolve-se um ensaio teórico de natureza bibliográfica e analítica, sustentado por literatura verificada sobre sobrecarga informacional, carga cognitiva, pensamento crítico, desordem informacional, raciocínio cívico on-line, intervenções de alfabetização midiática e educação digital, complementada por documentos normativos brasileiros e por marcos de organismos internacionais. A análise indica que o desafio contemporâneo não consiste em substituir a transmissão de conhecimentos por competências genéricas, mas em reorganizar a relação entre conhecimento acumulado e práticas de verificação. Argumenta-se que o julgamento crítico depende simultaneamente de saber substantivo, de critérios epistemológicos e de rotinas de investigação que permitam identificar autoria, comparar fontes, examinar evidências, reconhecer incertezas e revisar conclusões. Propõe-se, ao final, uma matriz de formação epistemológica com sete dimensões, acompanhada de uma progressão formativa e de implicações avaliativas, aplicável a diferentes níveis e modalidades de ensino, incluindo o tratamento da inteligência artificial generativa como objeto de verificação e não como autoridade epistêmica.

items.title: Effects of mimicry style, identity positioning, and description style on trust and usage intention in AI pet healthcare platforms
items.abstract: With the continuous advancement of artificial intelligence applications in the field of pet healthcare, AI pet medical platforms have gradually become important tools for pet health management. However, in contexts characterized by high emotional involvement and high uncertainty, users’ trust in and adoption of such platforms still face significant challenges. Based on trust calibration theory, uncertainty management theory, and the Computers Are Social Actors paradigm, this study adopts a 2 × 2 × 2 between-subjects experimental design to examine the effects of mimicry style (anthropomorphic design versus zoomorphic design), identity positioning (expert-authoritative versus friendly-companion), and description style (lay terminology versus professional terminology) on users’ cognitive trust, affective attachment, and usage intention. A total of 400 valid samples were collected, and the hypotheses were tested using analysis of variance and mediation analysis. The results indicate that zoomorphic design significantly enhances affective attachment and usage intention and exerts a partial mediating effect on usage intention through affective attachment and cognitive trust. Expert-authoritative identity positioning significantly increases cognitive trust and usage intention, whereas the mediating role of affective attachment is not significant. Descriptive style shows no significant direct effect on usage intention, but professional terminology exerts a mediating effect on usage intention through cognitive trust. In addition, a significant interaction effect is found between mimicry style and identity positioning. The findings suggest that user adoption of AI pet medical platforms is jointly driven by both affective and cognitive pathways, with cognitive trust playing a more central role in high-risk decision-making contexts. This study extends the application of the Computers Are Social Actors paradigm and trust calibration theory in the pet healthcare context and provides practical implications for the interface and communication design of AI pet medical platforms.

items.title: Enhancing Maritime Cyber Resilience: A Call for Comprehensive Training and Regulation
items.abstract: This article addresses the critical issues associated with maritime cyber-security and focusses on the training and education needed for maritime sector employees and professionals in the port sector. It provides essential context for understanding the increasing threat landscape, exemplified by a 900 per cent rise in cyber breaches targeting operational technology in ships and ports in 2023. It underscores the global impact of cyber threats, and highlights major incidents in ports worldwide. The escalating frequency of attacks on shipping lines, container terminals and national key points raises concerns about financial losses and potential risks to human life, alongside damage to infrastructure and the environment. We argue that the critical aspect of cyber resilience is the human factor, which is considered to be a potential weak link in cyber-security. We explore the importance of training the maritime workforce to enhance cyber resilience, analyse the scope of the training obligations imposed by the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code, and note gaps in the application of this framework in South Africa's Merchant Shipping (Maritime Security) Regulations, 2004. Furthermore, the non-mandatory guidelines to the ISPS Code lack both force of law and sufficient specificity. Against this background we emphasise the growing attention by regulators in the United States, European Union and United Kingdom to the vulnerabilities of cyber-physical systems in ports, and the need for specific regulations to address these risks. While acknowledging the existing regulations, we advocate the urgent development of a comprehensive port-sector cyber-security policy and guidelines in South Africa and the amendment of the existing regulations to include mandatory cyber-security provisions. In conclusion we emphasise the need for a coordinated effort in the South African port sector to promote cyber resiliency, understood as being the ability to identify, mitigate and respond to cyber threats effectively. We call for the integration of cyber-security into executive strategies, policies and procedures, and stress the importance of continuous learning and information sharing to create a resilient maritime industry.

items.title: Examining English Learning Demotivation Level of Indonesian First-Year University Students: A Comparative Study
items.abstract: Demotivation can undermine students’ engagement and persistence in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning, particularly during the transition to university, when first-year students encounter new academic and assessment demands. Understanding its sources is therefore important for supporting students’ adjustment and sustained engagement in English learning. The current study aimed to investigate the level of students’ demotivation in English learning, the dominant factors, and the differences based on gender and educational background. It focused on first-year students enrolled in an Islamic University in Madura that considers English as a compulsory and intensive course. This study was a quantitative research with a survey design. Demotivation questionnaires were adopted and modified from Sakai and Kikuchi (2009) and administered to 147 students through Google Forms. The findings revealed a moderate level of demotivation. Based on the reverse scale, in which lower scores indicate higher demotivation, test scores emerged as the most prominent demotivating factor (M = 3.03), followed by inadequate learning facilities (M = 3.16), learning contents and materials (M = 3.31), lack of intrinsic motivation (M = 3.33), and teacher competence and teaching styles (M = 3.50). A significant gender difference was found, with male students reporting higher demotivation (M = 3.10) than female students (M = 3.39), t(145) = 2.134, p = .035. In contrast, no significant difference was found across educational backgrounds, F(5, 141) = 1.068, p = .381. These findings highlight the importance of assessment experiences in first-year EFL demotivation and suggest the need for more supportive assessment practices during students’ transition to university English learning..

items.title: Fluent but unfounded: generative AI, cue–evidence decoupling and founder judgement
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can now produce, within minutes, a venture risk assessment that reads like the work of an experienced analyst. Whether founders, and the investors who read their documents, can still tell how much such an assessment rests on is an open question with consequences for entrepreneurship, finance and the governance of AI. This article develops a theory of cue–evidence decoupling. People judge the strength of evidence from cues such as fluency, structure and agreement, and generative AI supplies these cues whether or not the evidence is there. Because founders act when the uncertainty they perceive falls to a level they can accept, decoupling lowers perceived uncertainty without lowering actual uncertainty. It also weakens written venture materials as costly signals to investors. Because feedback in entrepreneurship is slow and noisy, founders should learn to correct for decoupling only slowly. To make the theory testable before outcomes are known, the article draws on risk science to define the knowledge-strength gap: the number of strength-of-knowledge criteria on which a founder rates an AI-assisted risk assessment as better supported than blind raters judge a normalised version of it to be. Eight propositions specify when the gap widens (novel ventures; estimating rather than listing risks), when it narrows (an AI critic; feedback on past estimates), how it raises resource commitment and how disclosure of AI use shifts investors' errors. Each proposition is paired with a randomised test and a result that would refute it. The theory implies that AI may mislead founders most where they need it most. It recasts the debate on AI and Knightian uncertainty as a question about founders' beliefs, and it suggests that safeguards for AI-assisted decisions, including transparency rules, should target the grounds of confidence and not only the accuracy of AI output.

items.title: From Generative AI to Agentic AI in Higher Education: A Behavioural Experiment on Delegation Using Diffusion of Innovations
items.abstract: In higher education, agentic AI goes beyond drafting content to creating learning management system (LMS) artefacts and scheduling releases under teacher oversight. Adoption research has modelled intention towards tools that draft rather than act, leaving delegation to a system that acts unobserved. This study estimated the effect of assignment to an action-taking scenario on teachers’ workflow choices, using Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) theory to explain delegation within that scenario. We randomly assigned 290 university teachers to a GenAI drafting-only condition (n = 140) or an LMS-integrated agentic condition (n = 150); each made step-by-step choices in a scenario-based six-step quiz workflow combining content drafting with student-facing platform actions. Teachers assigned to the agentic scenario chose AI support for more steps (d = 0.65), but the gain sat almost entirely on content drafting (d = 0.99) and was negligible for platform actions (d = 0.12). This content–platform boundary was sharp: 92% chose to delegate question writing, while 77% chose to schedule releases manually. Most chose limited autonomy (48% selected draft-only, 35% selected approval-gated publishing, 5% selected auto-publish). The five DOI attributes and controls explained substantial variance in an Agentic Use Behaviour Index (AUBI) of delegation, autonomy, and permissions (R2 = 0.65). Complexity, understood as oversight burden, was negatively associated with AUBI, and its association with non-manual engagement was stronger in the agentic scenario; observability was not significant. The direction of the AUBI results held across four weightings and count and ordinal models, and exploratory clustering suggested four adopter profiles forming a permission ladder. Extending DOI from tool adoption to task delegation, the results favour draft-first defaults, approval gates, and staged permissions, with field replication using LMS logs a priority.

items.title: From hobbies to examination progression: a study of art-track candidates' motivations for participating in non-academic tutoring
items.abstract: Non-academic tutoring is an important channel through which families help their children accumulate cultural capital. Existing studies have mostly analysed parental motivations from a static perspective, and few have examined how students' motivations change across educational stages. Based on in-depth interviews with 22 art-track candidates, this article finds that their motivations for participating in arts tutoring show a marked shift from value rationality to instrumental rationality. In primary school and before, the intrinsic motivation of personal interest dominated their participation in interest classes. At the two key educational transitions of the high school entrance examination (zhongkao) and the college entrance examination (gaokao), they chose to study art majors out of the extrinsic motivation of examination progression. In this process, the form of tutoring they attended shifted from arts interest classes to professional intensive training classes, and the learning content was replaced by examination subjects for art majors.

items.title: From technology to meaningful learning: cognitive, communicative, and cross-cultural effects of AI integration in bilingual education
items.abstract: Background Integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in bilingual education is increasingly consequential for students' cognitive engagement and professional communication, yet prior research has examined these outcomes largely in isolation. Whether learning engagement and cross-cultural competence (CCC) operate as simultaneous, parallel indirect pathways linking AI integration to perceived learning effectiveness and business communication skill remains underexamined, and cultural intelligence has rarely been modeled as a boundary condition on the intercultural pathway. Methods Drawing on a cross-sectional dataset of 604 bilingual education students across 13 universities in China, this study integrated the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology, Social Cognitive Theory, and Cultural Intelligence Theory within a single framework. Ordinary least squares regression with HC3 robust standard errors and partial least squares structural equation modeling with bootstrap-based indirect effect and latent moderation analyses were employed. Results All three indirect pathways were statistically supported: AI → learning engagement → perceived learning effectiveness (β = 0.191), AI → CCC → business communication skill (β = 0.278), and AI → CCC → perceived learning effectiveness (β = 0.202), each carrying a larger share of the AI-outcome association than the corresponding direct path. The model explained 28.38% of variance in learning engagement, 34.33% in CCC, 40.85% in business communication skill, and 47.28% in perceived learning effectiveness. Cultural intelligence positively moderated the AI → CCC association (β = 0.200), with simple slopes rising from 0.298 at low cultural intelligence to 0.697 at high cultural intelligence. Conclusion AI integration is associated with distal learning and communication outcomes predominantly through engagement-related and intercultural mechanisms, with cultural intelligence conditioning the strength of the intercultural pathway. These findings suggest that AI funding in bilingual education should be conditioned on process metrics, learning engagement and intercultural capability, rather than on tool procurement alone. Structured intercultural scaffolding should be required as an accreditation condition for AI-supported bilingual courses, and cultural intelligence screening at program entry with tiered support for lower-cultural-intelligence learners warrants consideration, given that the benefits of AI-supported learning are non-uniform across learners.

items.title: Geometric Properties of Human High-Performing Buildings: A Review of the Evidence and the Implications for Practice
items.abstract: Building performance is conventionally assessed in structural, thermal, energy, and functional terms, while architectural character is treated as a matter of taste. Yet a growing body of research suggests that the geometric characteristics of buildings also affect performance experienced directly by people—perceptual engagement, restoration and well-being, perceived safety, social affordance, and patterns of movement and use—both within buildings and in adjoining streets and public spaces. This paper reviews that evidence and develops a conceptual model and theoretical account of how the relevant characteristics arise. Drawing on environmental psychology, experimental aesthetics, neuroaesthetics, urban design, and the mathematics of form, it identifies recurring geometric characteristics associated with favorable human responses, centered on symmetry and symmetry-breaking, multiscale organization, and contextual relationship. It proposes that these are traces of generative processes rather than attributes of style, and it introduces “deep symmetry”: a progression of correspondence from the isolated object through scale and context to the perceiving human participant, with a candidate mechanism grounded in embodied perception and processing fluency. The framework reframes stylistic debates as questions of human performance, geometry, and process, and sets out a falsifiable research agenda, candidate measures, and broader implications for practice.

items.title: Hegemonic Masculinity, Motivation and Aggression Among Collegiate Male Athletes: A Quantitative Correlational Study
items.abstract: This study examined the relationship among hegemonic masculinity, sports motivation, and aggression among collegiate male athletes in the satellite campuses of Bukidnon State University. Specifically, it determined the level of adherence to hegemonic masculinity in terms of emotional control, self-reliance, risk-taking, winning, and heterosexual self-presentation; assessed sports motivation based on intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and amotivation; and identified aggression in sports through behavioral and emotional aggression. The study employed a quantitative correlational research design involving 53 male collegiate athletes selected through purposive sampling. Data were gathered using adopted and validated survey instruments, including measures of masculine norms, sports motivation, and aggression. Descriptive statistics and correlational analysis were utilized to analyze the data and determine the relationships among variables. The findings revealed that masculine identity, motivational factors, and aggressive tendencies are interconnected aspects of athletes’ experiences. The study highlighted that competitive orientations and certain masculine expectations may influence athletes’ emotional regulation and behavioral responses during sports participation. The results provided empirical evidence for developing a gender-sensitive intervention program focused on promoting healthy masculinity, self-determined motivation, emotional regulation, sportsmanship, and responsible athletic behavior. The study contributes to understanding the psychological and social factors shaping male collegiate athletes within a local sports context.

items.title: Hopes and fears: first year geoscience students encounter with academia
items.abstract: Through interviews and questionnaires, we investigate geoscience students’ motivations, expectations and concerns at the start of the bachelor programme at the University of Oslo, Norway, and how these change as the students encounter the courses, peers, staff and study environment in their first year. Students begin with a mix of extrinsic and intrinsic motivations that become more self-determined over the first year. Initially, they are eager to learn but unsure they can succeed; by year’s end doubts shift toward the applicability of their education and future job prospects. Students hope to build relationships and make friends and fear that they will not; although these fears subside quickly for most, students consistently emphasize the importance of positive relationships. Though greater self-determination and better relationships typically are viewed as something positive, for some students it appears that increased self-determination is accompanied by heightened sensitivity to academic difficulties, teacher expectations, and the implications of success or failure. Though institutional shortcomings were not cited as reasons for dropping out by participants in this study, the findings highlight opportunities to support student success and retention by addressing self-efficacy, study technique, perceived relevance, and workload management.

items.title: How Distributed, Consensus-Free Folklore Enables Transfeminine Disposability on Bluesky
items.abstract: Bluesky, a novel social networking platform, offers a space with valuable community ties for transfeminine individuals. At the same time, though, these communities are not free of intracommunity conflict, particularly conflict predicated on a transmisogynistic politics of disposability. We conduct a grounded theory interview study with 13 transfeminine Bluesky users, finding that transfeminine individuals experience attacks predicated on their disposability that are primarily driven by a form of disinformation we call distributed, consensus-free (DCF) folklore. DCF folklore turns communities against users who have previously provided crucial labor to those same communities; we frame it as an networked phenomenon that results from extant dynamics and affordances on the platform. In order to mitigate the harms done by the circulation of this folklore, we conclude by discussing opportunities for tools to more effectively support bottom-up moderation that affords for nuance and contextualization.

items.title: How is Work-Related Fatigue Defined and Measured in Anaesthesiology, Intensive Care and Emergency Medicine? A Scoping Review Protocol
items.abstract: Fatigue among clinical staff working in anaesthesiology, intensive care and emergency medicine is widely regarded as a determinant of both patient safety and staff well-being. Shift work, night duty and on-call commitments are structural features of these specialties, and the resulting sleep loss and circadian disruption are consistently discussed as sources of impaired performance, reduced vigilance and adverse occupational health outcomes. Despite this attention, the literature does not converge on a single operationalisation of the construct. Fatigue is variously described as a subjective state, a performance decrement, a consequence of sleep debt, or a dimension of burnout, and it is assessed with instruments that were developed for different purposes and different populations. Subjective questionnaires, objective psychomotor testing, actigraphy and qualitative accounts coexist in the same body of literature, frequently without explicit justification for the chosen approach. Terms such as fatigue, sleepiness and emotional exhaustion are used interchangeably in some reports and as distinct constructs in others. This heterogeneity limits comparability across studies and complicates the design of interventional research. A scoping review is the appropriate design here because the objective is to map the conceptual and methodological landscape rather than to estimate the effect of a defined intervention on a defined outcome. Consistent with JBI guidance, no critical appraisal of individual sources is planned, as the aim is to characterise the breadth of definitions and measurement approaches in use, not to grade the strength of evidence.

items.title: Human-AI collaborative intelligence: a framework for enhancing employee engagement through trust-mediated technology acceptance in digital workplaces
items.abstract: Purpose: The study aimed to assess the mediating effect of trust and task-technology fit in human-AI collaboration environments in employee engagement in digital workplaces. Design/methodology/approach: A mixed-methods study design was used with 687 employees in various industries. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to test the relationships among the capabilities of the AI system, trust, and task-technology fit, as well as relationships between employee engagement and trust. 42 participants in qualitative interviews gave further insights into the interaction patterns between humans and AI. Results: The results show that the capabilities of AI systems substantially contribute to employee engagement via their role of full mediation, namely through their mediation by trust in AI systems (indirect effect = 0.31, p < 0.001) and task-technology fit (indirect effect = 0.27, p < 0.001). The indirect effects of AI Design Quality in the mediation model through trust (0.32) and task-technology fit (0.29) are comparable, resulting in total effects of β = 0.66, p < 0.001. The study shows that design and customization of AI are key factors in boosting employee trust and engagement, and transparency is key to this. Research limitations/implications: Because this was a cross-sectional study, causal inferences are limited. Longitudinal research is needed to investigate the dynamic nature of human-AI interaction in a changing work environment. Practical implications: It is essential for organisations to focus on the transparency of AI, offer thorough training and ensure that tasks and technology align well to maximise the benefits of employee engagement from the implementation of AI. Originality/value: It offers a first comprehensive framework that integrates the Technology Acceptance Model, Job Demands-Resources theory and Human-AI Interaction to gain insights into the impact of AI on employee engagement.

items.title: Human-Centered Corrective Control in Semi-Automatic Construction Machinery: Enhancing Stability and Operator Intent Integration
items.abstract: Semi-automatic piloting combines prerecorded machine motion with operator corrections, but how corrective inputs evolve across repeated interactions remains unclear. We examined corrective lever inputs during simulated grading and loading with two skilled excavator operators. Each operator corrected their own and the other operator’s recorded actions, with corrections either immediately applied (Apply) or recorded without affecting the current motion (No Apply). Cycle-level root mean square (RMS) values summarized corrective-input magnitude, and generalized estimating equations examined temporal trends. RMS generally decreased during grading under Apply but tended to increase during loading, particularly along the Swing axis. The grading model detected feedback-dependent slopes, whereas neither task model detected baseline-source-dependent slopes. These findings do not establish equivalence between baseline sources, and the task comparison remains descriptive. Because the experiment involved two operators, fixed task order, and a simulator, the results are exploratory. Estimates remain conditional on the assumed independence between repeated series from the same operator. items.title: Idealizing energy democracy in the European semi-periphery: lithium mining, solar energy and fiction
items.abstract: Abstract Background The EU Green Deal aims to turn Europe into the first carbon neutral continent by 2050. However, criticisms of the hegemonic versions of this energy transition have focused on the top-down, asymmetric and corporate dimensions that often view local communities as barriers to the swift implementation of renewable energy infrastructures. Indeed, current scholarship argues that the energy transition is only maximizing the contradictions of neoliberal capitalism as the rapid rollout of green technologies increases North/South asymmetries, thereby fostering capital accumulation, green grabbing and ecocide. Research findings have furthermore argued that semi-peripheral countries such as Portugal are disproportionately affected by these negative impacts of the EU Green Deal. This paper explores two of the leading environmental controversies in the Portuguese context stemming directly from the prevailing energy transition – lithium mining in northern Portugal and plans to construct a large solar power plant in the Alentejo. Results The controversial lithium mining and solar energy projects prioritise corporate ownership, the centralization of renewable energy production, the marginalization of local communities as well as producing large green sacrifice zones and raising issues around energy democracy. This paper explores the role of fiction in the idealization of counter-hegemonic alternatives to the energy transition in keeping with the energy democracy theoretical framework. Highlighting some of the main principles of energy democracy – such as democratic control over energy systems, the redistribution of political-economic power, the universal right to renewable energy and social justice – this article puts forward a fictional scenario, set in 2035, in an ecovillage in Central Portugal. Through exploring the ways in which this fictional community put its own energy transition into practice, the paper sketches a speculative future aligned with the theoretical and sociopolitical concerns around energy democracy. Conclusion Our research suggests fiction might support the imagination of utopian versions of energy futures, articulating energy democracy principles with specific sociotechnical endeavours, problematizing the climate realism underpinning the predominant energy transitions. In this sense, fiction may play an important role in idealizing democratic energy transitions, combining the “what if” of socio-literary techniques with the normative demands and contradictions of low-carbon futures.

items.abstract: The practical significance of this study lies in the detailed description of the didactic conditions under which Excel-based digital tools can be effectively used to overcome formalism in students' knowledge acquisition. By examining the interdisciplinary integration of mathematics, geography, and computer science, the study demonstrates how abstract mathematical concepts, including formulas, functions, and percentages, as well as complex geographical indicators such as temperature and precipitation patterns, can be transformed into interactive visual representations within the Excel environment. Such an approach promotes visual-spatial thinking, increases students' intrinsic motivation and cognitive engagement, and facilitates the transition from rote memorization to meaningful experimentation and independent knowledge construction.

items.title: Is gig work the same for everyone? Psychosocial job demands, resources, and well-being in platform work across Europe: evidence from the GIG-OSH study
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Research on digital platform work increasingly highlights unclear employment arrangements and pressures related to algorithmic management. This study aimed to describe psychosocial working conditions in web-based and on-location gig work using the job demands‑resources (JD-R) model and examine associations between job demands, job resources, factors preventing resource depletion (FPRD), and health outcomes among platform workers. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Cross-sectional data were drawn from the GIG-OSH project conducted in 7 European countries (Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Poland, Spain, Sweden, and the United Kingdom). Data were collected through an online survey in November 2023 - April 2024. The analytic sample comprised 3299 platform workers (1476 on-location, 1823 web-based). A project-specific questionnaire assessed socio-demographic characteristics, employment conditions, workload, occupational safety and health hazards, psychosocial working conditions, algorithmic management, and health outcomes. Psychosocial factors were classified as job demands, job resources, or FPRD within an extended JD-R framework. RESULTS: Platform work was characterized by an imbalance between job demands and resources, particularly among onlocation workers. Compared with web-based workers, they reported greater exposure to emotionally disturbing situations, aggression, violence, discrimination, and sexual harassment. Working alone was common in both groups but more prevalent in web-based work. Factors preventing resource depletion indicators, especially absence of fines and protection against fraudulent bookings, were more favourable in web-based work. Higher job demands were significantly associated with poorer health outcomes, with emotionally disturbing situations showing the strongest effect. Job resources demonstrated modest protective associations, whereas FPRD indicators, particularly not working while ill, were consistently associated with better health. CONCLUSIONS: Platform work involves substantial psychosocial risks linked to poorer well-being and health, supporting the JD-R model. Distinct psychosocial profiles of web-based and on-location work highlight the need for targeted occupational health and platform policy interventions. Int J Occup Med Environ Health. 2026;39(5).

items.title: Job Autonomy and Employee Adaptation to Digital and AI-Enabled Tools in Vietnamese SMEs: A Conceptual Model with Cultural Orientations and Digital Leadership as Moderators
items.abstract: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Vietnam are adopting digital and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools under strong policy encouragement, but adoption at firm level does not guarantee adaptation at employee level. Job autonomy is widely recommended as a work design condition for such adaptation; most of the supporting evidence, however, comes from low power distance, individualist settings. This paper develops a conceptual model of how job autonomy relates to employees' technology adaptation behaviour in Vietnamese SMEs and of the conditions under which that relationship holds. Drawing on the job characteristics model, self-determination theory, diffusion of innovations, the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology and leader–member exchange theory, the model treats two individual-level cultural orientations, power distance orientation and harmony–face concern, as moderators that weaken the autonomy–adaptation link, and treats digital leadership as a moderator that strengthens it and partly compensates for the cultural dampening. Five propositions are derived. A research design is specified that is suited to the small samples typical of SME studies: a two-wave employee–supervisor survey, Bayesian structural equation modelling with weakly informative priors, and multi-group comparison with prior tests of measurement invariance. The model contributes a culturally situated account of autonomy effects to the human resource management (HRM) literature on digital transformation and offers SME managers and policy makers guidance on pairing autonomy with leader endorsement and group-based learning when introducing AI-enabled tools.

items.title: Job Autonomy and Subjective Well-Being Among University Faculty
items.abstract: University faculty frequently navigate competing demands across their professional and family roles, making job autonomy an important yet complex resource for well-being. Although prior research has established a positive association between job autonomy and employee well-being, less is known about the work–family processes through which autonomy contributes to faculty well-being and how these processes may vary by gender. Drawing on Conservation of Resources Theory, we employed a mixed-methods study to examine the relationship between job autonomy and university faculty’s subjective well-being and further explored the boundary and work–family processes underlying this relationship. Study 1 used survey data from 206 university faculty members in China and tested mediation and moderated mediation models. The results showed that job autonomy was positively associated with subjective well-being, with boundary control and work–family balance serving as independent and sequential mediators. Gender further moderated the relationship between job autonomy and work–family balance, such that the positive association was stronger among female faculty. Study 2 used semi-structured interviews with ten university faculty members to further explain these quantitative findings. The qualitative findings showed that faculty used autonomy to proactively coordinate work and family demands, while autonomy could also increase work permeability and self-regulatory demands. Together, the findings demonstrate that job autonomy is both a resource for well-being and a condition that reshapes how faculty manage work–family boundaries, highlighting the importance of gender and contextual responsibilities in understanding its consequences.

items.title: Job performance, job satisfaction, and workload as correlates of occupational self-efficacy in educators from rural areas of Peru
items.abstract: Objective To examine the associations of job performance, job satisfaction, and workload with occupational self-efficacy among educators in rural areas of Peru. Materials and methods A cross-sectional, explanatory-correlational study with latent variables was conducted using a non-probability sample of 457 educators from rural areas of Puno, Peru, with a mean age of 44 years; the majority were women (57.3%). The Occupational Self-Efficacy Scale–Short Form (OSS-SF), Individual Work Performance Scale, Warr, Cook, and Wall Job Satisfaction Scale, and Workload Scale (ECT) were administered. All variables were assessed simultaneously, at a single time point, through self-report questionnaires. Structural equation modeling (SEM) with the weighted least squares mean and variance adjusted (WLSMV) estimator was used to estimate the associations among the study variables. Results Job performance was the only variable showing a significant, positive, and moderate direct association with occupational self-efficacy ( β = 0.68); together, the three variables explained 43% of its variance ( R 2 = 0.43). Workload was negatively correlated with job performance ( r = −0.31) and job satisfaction ( r = −0.26), whereas job performance was positively correlated with job satisfaction ( r = 0.55). In contrast, workload ( β = −0.03) and job satisfaction ( β = −0.05) did not show significant direct associations with occupational self-efficacy. Conclusion Self-perceived job performance was the only variable uniquely associated with occupational self-efficacy and was positively associated with job satisfaction among educators in rural areas. In contrast, workload was negatively associated with both job performance and job satisfaction, without a significant direct association with occupational self-efficacy. Given the cross-sectional design, these associations should not be interpreted as causal; nonetheless, supporting teachers’ job performance and improving working conditions may be promising targets to promote wellbeing and educational quality, which should be examined in longitudinal and intervention studies.

items.title: Mapping vocational e-learning research: A bibliometric analysis
items.abstract: Vocational e-learning has become increasingly important as vocational education systems respond to digital transformation, changing labour-market demands, and the need for flexible skills development. However, research on vocational e-learning remains scattered across educational technology, vocational education, vocational training, workforce development, and professional skills development. This study maps the evolution, knowledge architecture, and thematic structure of vocational e-learning research through a bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in the Web of Science. A topic search was conducted on April 28, 2026, without setting a publication year limit. After restricting the results to English-language journal articles, 1,014 records were retained for analysis. Publication trend analysis, citation analysis, country-level co-authorship analysis, co-citation analysis, and author keyword co-occurrence analysis were conducted using VOSviewer. The findings show that vocational e-learning research gradually expanded after 2006 and accelerated after 2019, reaching a publication peak in 2022. The United States, England, and the People’s Republic of China were among the main contributors, although national-level collaboration remained uneven. Co-citation analysis revealed five intellectual clusters related to online and blended learning foundations, emergency online learning, vocational and simulation-based training, technology acceptance, and digital pedagogy or technology-enhanced learning. items.title: Motivational Practices and Employee Productivity in India's Power Sector: A Comparative Study of Public and Private Companies Using BRSR Disclosures
items.abstract: Motivation practices and employee productivity were analysed in five central public sector power companies and four private power companies using the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reports and Financial Results of the companies for the financial year 2024-2025. Data was used to build proxies for job security, training, performance feedback, welfare and safety along with productivity which was measured as revenue and profit per employee. Mann-Whitney U tests and Spearman correlation tests were applied to the data. Public companies spent more on employee welfare and had lower attrition. Private companies spent more on employee training. None of these differences including productivity were significant at the 5% levels. The two sectors have different HR motivational models for similar productivity output. This has implications on HR policy in the energy transition.

items.title: Musculoskeletal Pain and Postural Abnormalities among Lebanese University Students: Prevalence and Correlates from a Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Background Musculoskeletal (MSK) pain is a major global health concern and is increasingly recognized among university students due to prolonged sedentary behavior, extensive digital device use, and academic demands. In Lebanon, data on MSK pain within this population remain limited. This study aims to determine the prevalence of MSK pain and postural abnormalities among Lebanese university students and to identify demographic, academic, lifestyle, and health-related factors associated with MSK pain. Methods A cross-sectional study using the Extended Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ-E) and the Internet Addiction Test (IAT) was conducted among 396 university students from higher education institutions across Lebanon. Participants completed a structured questionnaire incorporating these validated instruments, along with questions on sociodemographic characteristics, academic behaviors, ergonomic practices, lifestyle factors, and medical conditions. Descriptive statistics, bivariate analyses, multivariable logistic regression, and multiple linear regression were performed. Results The findings indicate a high lifetime prevalence of MSK pain, particularly in the neck (68.7%), lower back (69.2%), and shoulders (60.9%). In multivariable analysis, female sex is independently associated with higher odds of MSK pain across multiple regions (aOR = 1.9–2.8, 95% CI: 1.0–5.3, p < 0.05). Self-perceived poor posture shows a strong association with lower back pain (aOR = 2.0, 95% CI: 1.01–4.14, p < 0.05), upper back pain, wrist/hand pain, and overall pain burden. Sleep disorders (aOR = 2.3–3.0, 95% CI: 1.03–7.02, p < 0.05) and migraine (aOR = 2.3, 95% CI: 1.26–4.05, p < 0.01) are also independently associated with increased MSK pain. In linear regression, male sex is associated with a lower overall pain score (β = −0.16, p < 0.01), while poor posture and comorbid conditions remain significant predictors of higher pain scores. Conclusion MSK pain is highly prevalent among Lebanese university students and is influenced by a combination of ergonomic, academic, lifestyle, and health-related factors. These findings highlight the importance of implementing university-based prevention strategies that promote ergonomic awareness, healthy study behaviors, and student well-being to reduce the burden of MSK pain.

items.title: Neural Representations as New Modes of Interactivity
items.abstract: Human-AI interaction today runs almost entirely through prompts and outputs, keeping AI systems opaque to general users. We introduce Neural Representation Interaction (NRI), a paradigm that treats the internal representations of neural networks as an interaction material people can inspect, steer, and edit. Situating NRI alongside graphical, tangible, and bio-computer interaction, we argue that the concepts and algorithms models encode internally offer representational affordances for richer human-AI interaction. We synthesize actionable mechanistic interpretability methods and, drawing on General Morphological Analysis, construct a design space spanning Interaction, Target, Referent, and Purpose. Mapping existing interfaces onto this space reveals that most serve expert auditors, while few support lay users. We then present speculative applications in education, personal user modeling, and hiring audits, and discuss design principles, limitations, and sociotechnical risks. NRI offers HCI researchers abstractions for designing interactions that work with AI computation rather than only through its inputs and outputs.

items.title: Occupational Safety Knowledge and Personal Protective Equipment Practices among Retail Butchers in the Cauvery Delta Region of Tamil Nadu, India
items.abstract: Retail butchers encounter occupational hazards associated with sharp instruments and meat handling. This cross-sectional survey assessed occupational health and safety knowledge, personal protective equipment (PPE) knowledge and reported use, and injury-prevention awareness among 200 retail butchers in the Cauvery Delta region of Tamil Nadu, India, during May–June 2026. The study covered Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam and Mayiladuthurai districts and used a structured questionnaire containing 29 occupational health and safety items. Knowledge scores were classified as poor (0–14), moderate (15–21) or good (22–29). Of the respondents, 72 (36.0%) reported previous formal occupational-safety training and 128 (64.0%) reported none. Knowledge of the protective roles of aprons and gloves was reported by 75.0% and 73.0%, respectively, whereas reported use was 61.0% and 42.0%, respectively. These figures derive from separate knowledge and use items and do not establish individual-level compliance. Safe knife handling, immediate first aid and prompt injury reporting were recognised by 79.0%, 77.0% and 64.0% of respondents, respectively. Overall, 32.0% had good knowledge, 41.0% moderate knowledge and 27.0% poor knowledge. Good knowledge was recorded for 43.1% of trained respondents and 25.8% of untrained respondents. Knowledge category was associated with previous training (Pearson’s χ²(2, N = 200) = 8.76, p = 0.013). The findings identify differences between aggregate knowledge and self-reported use measures and an association between previous training and knowledge, without demonstrating causality.

items.title: Off- Campus Learning Experience and Personality Development of Swimming Team: Inputs for Policy Insights
items.abstract: Abstract. This study examined the off-campus learning experiences and personal development of swimming team members under curriculum innovation initiatives in the Division of Agusan del Sur to inform policy insights. It assessed off-campus learning experiences in terms of skill development, sportsmanship and teamwork, discipline and time management, motivation and self-confidence, and academic responsibility; determined the extent of development across emotional, behavioral, cognitive, and social dimensions; and examined the relationships among these variables. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed. The participants were 34 Grade 6 swimming team members selected through total enumeration. Data were gathered using a structured questionnaire and analyzed through frequency and percentage, weighted mean, and Spearman rank-order correlation. Results showed effective off-campus learning experiences. Motivation and self-confidence obtained the highest mean (4.50), followed by sportsmanship and teamwork (4.49), discipline and time management (4.36), academic responsibility (4.31), and skill development (4.05). Among the measured dimensions, cognitive engagement obtained the highest mean (4.15), followed by behavioral (4.14), emotional (4.04), and social development (approximately 4.02). Most relationships between off-campus learning experiences and developmental dimensions were not statistically significant. Sportsmanship and teamwork showed inverse associations with behavioral engagement (ρ = −.355, p = .040) and social engagement (ρ = −.397, p = .020) at the unadjusted level. However, neither association remained statistically significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons. The study proposed an Enhanced Off-Campus Learning Experience and Learner Development Policy to strengthen structured learning, holistic development, academic coordination, safety, inclusion, and regular monitoring. items.title: Perceived workload and associated organizational factors among healthcare professionals in emergency departments of referral hospitals in Conakry, Guinea: a multicenter cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background Workload affects occupational health, staff well-being and quality of care. Emergency departments are particularly demanding, especially in resource-limited settings. This study assessed perceived workload and associated organizational and professional factors among healthcare professionals working in referral hospital emergency departments in Conakry, Guinea. Methods We conducted a multicenter analytical cross-sectional study from March 2 to June 2, 2026, in the emergency departments of Donka University Hospital, Ignace Deen University Hospital and the Sino-Guinean Hospital. Eligible physicians and nurses were exhaustively recruited. Perceived workload was measured using the NASA Task Load Index, and associated factors were examined using bivariate analyses and multiple linear regression. Results A total of 146 healthcare professionals were included; the median age was 32 years, and nurses represented 58.9% of participants. The median weekly working time was 56 hours. The overall NASA-TLX score indicated a high perceived workload, mainly driven by mental demand, physical demand and overall effort. In multivariable analysis, being aged 30–39 years was associated with a higher workload score, whereas perceived adequate staffing was associated with a lower score. A moderate work atmosphere was also associated with increased workload compared with a good work atmosphere. Conclusions Perceived workload among emergency department healthcare professionals in Conakry was high and was mainly associated with organizational determinants, particularly staffing adequacy and work atmosphere. Interventions should strengthen human resources, improve the work environment and help prevent psychosocial risks. Trial registration: Not applicable. This study was an observational cross-sectional survey and did not evaluate a health care intervention on human participants.

items.title: Pilot Study on Scale Reliability and Model Validity for Human and Technological Factors Influencing Smart Transportation Service Performance
items.abstract: This pilot study is to test the reliability of measurement scales and the validity of the research model used to study human and technological factors that impact smart transportation service performance. A quantitative method was used in which a structured questionnaire was used to gather data from a population of 30 participants relevant to the smart transportation context in Amman, Jordan. The study aims to evaluate the internal consistency of the measurement items in each of the three internal dimensions of the study, of which the three dimensions of the human factor (Smart Transportation Awareness, Perceived Safety, Social Influence) and three dimensions of the technological factor (Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, Facilitating Condition, System Integration, and Data Privacy) are examined, and to confirm the correctness of the relations of constructs in the model, namely Smart Transportation Service Performance. The findings show satisfactory reliability of all the measurement scales and acceptable validity of the model, which allows us to use the model in further large-scale empirical studies. The result of this pilot study is considered to be a methodological foundation for further research and the strength of the developed research instrument for the study of the performance of smart transportation services.

items.title: Point-of-Care Electroanalytical Technologies for Lithium Carbonate Monitoring in Bipolar Affective Disorders
items.abstract: Abstract Lithium (Li), administered as lithium salts such as lithium carbonate (Li2CO3), remains a gold-standard maintenance treatment for bipolar affective disorder (bipolar disorder), but its narrow therapeutic index requires regular monitoring of lithium−ion (Li+) concentrations. This review critically examines electroanalytical strategies for decentralized Li measurement, including conventional electrodes, screen-printed electrodes, wearable platforms, and minimally invasive sampling. Attention is given to ion-selective recognition, manganese (Mn)-spinel intercalation materials, matrix effects, and the evidence supporting saliva, sweat, interstitial fluid, and capillary blood. The available literature supports these matrices as promising adjuncts but not as universal replacements for standardized venous testing. Their clinical use still requires paired matrix validation, control of sampling time and environmental effects, long-term sensor stability studies, and explicit confirmatory testing rules for suspected toxicity. Laser-induced graphene and fused deposition modeling are therefore discussed only as enabling fabrication concepts rather than as established Li-sensing technologies. Finally, the review outlines regulatory, human factor, connectivity, and healthcare integration requirements that must be addressed before wearable or home-use Li devices can support routine care.

items.title: Reduced-Port Robotic Living Donor Nephrectomy Using the da Vinci Xi Platform: A Comparative Cohort Study of SP+1 RDN, Multi-port Robotic, and Laparoendoscopic Single-Site Techniques
items.abstract: Background Living donor nephrectomy is performed in healthy individuals and therefore demands a particularly high safety threshold. Robotic donor nephrectomy may improve visualization, dexterity, and ergonomics, while reduced-port approaches seek to decrease abdominal wall trauma. Dedicated da Vinci SP platforms enable true single-port robotic surgery but are not universally available. We evaluated a single-port-plus-one (SP + 1 RDN) configuration performed with the conventional da Vinci Xi platform and compared it with laparoendoscopic single-site donor nephrectomy (LESS-DN) and conventional multi-port robotic donor nephrectomy (RDN). Methods This retrospective single-centre cohort included 808 living kidney donors in a prospectively maintained institutional database. Only 3 surgical techniques were included: 59 Xi SP + 1 RDN, 706 LESS-DN, and 43 multi-port RDN. items.title: Serum Creatinine Levels among Motorcycle Workshop Mechanics in Carbon Monoxide-Prone Workplaces: A Photometric Study
items.abstract: Motorcycle workshop mechanics work in environments where vehicle exhaust may accumulate, particularly in workshops located near dense traffic and with limited ventilation. Carbon monoxide (CO) is not directly measured in this study; therefore, daily working hours and years of employment are used as occupational indicators of possible long-term exposure. This descriptive cross-sectional study analyzed serum creatinine levels among 30 motorcycle workshop mechanics on Jalan Riau, Pekanbaru. Respondents were selected by purposive sampling based on predefined eligibility criteria. Venous blood was collected, processed into serum, and analyzed using an Optiva photometer with a Glory Diagnostics enzymatic creatinine kit at 510 nm. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize creatinine distribution by age, daily working duration, and length of employment. The results showed that 17 respondents (56.67%) had serum creatinine levels above the reference range (>1.3 mg/dL), while 13 respondents (43.33%) had normal levels (0.7-1.3 mg/dL). Increased creatinine levels were more frequent among mechanics working 12 hours/day (75%) than among those working 8 hours/day (20%), and were also more common in respondents aged 30 years or older and those with more than 10 years of employment. These findings suggest that mechanics with longer occupational contact in CO-prone workshop environments may have a higher proportion of elevated serum creatinine. However, because ambient CO or carboxyhemoglobin was not measured, the results should be interpreted as an occupational-health screening finding rather than evidence of direct causality. Improved ventilation, routine health monitoring, and occupational safety education are recommended.

items.title: Smart Underwear System Based on Real-Time Strain Gauge Measurement of Nocturnal Penile Tumescence (NPT) and Optimal Coital Timing Prediction Algorithm: Monetizing the 'Morning Glory'
items.abstract: Healthy adult males experience nocturnal penile tumescence (NPT) 3 to 5 times per night during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. Throughout human history, this substantial biomechanical energy has remained entirely unmonetized and squandered in unconsciousness. Building upon the pioneering textile-urological investigations of Shafik (2007 Ig Nobel Prize in Medicine), this study introduces the design and N=1 proof-of-concept evaluation of 'Smart Briefs v1.0'—an ergonomic wearable system integrating carbon nanotube (CNT) stretchable conductive fabric, a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) piezoelectric tenting-pressure sensor, and a negative temperature coefficient (NTC) scrotal thermistor. Real-time circumferential strain, axial rigidity, and duration are transmitted via Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) to a smartphone application. We formulate the Golden-Time Index (GTI) algorithm, which filters out bladder-filling reflex tumescence (Morning-After-Pee Syndrome, MAPS) and sleep-posture artifacts to identify optimal physiological windows for coitus. A 28-night single-subject self-experimentation protocol demonstrated a 97.9% reduction in prone-position false alarms ("The 03:00 AM Crisis") via 3-axis gyroscope posture compensation. By converting unconscious nocturnal physiological events into actionable push notifications and meteorological intimacy forecasts, this research advances domestic reproductive timing from intuitive guesswork to precision data science.

items.title: Stress Levels and Teaching Performance of Secondary English Teachers in Bantayan, Cebu Province
items.abstract: This study examined occupational stress and teaching performance among 100 secondary English teachers from 14 schools on Bantayan Island, Cebu Province, during the 2024-2025 academic year. A descriptive-comparative and correlational research design was employed. Data were collected using a perceived work stress questionnaire and existing Classroom Observation Tool ratings. The findings indicated a moderate overall stress level, with work overload and role ambiguity emerging as prominent workplace concerns. Teachers demonstrated high intrinsic motivation, moderate extrinsic motivation, and generally very satisfactory to outstanding teaching performance. Most demographic and professional characteristics showed no statistically significant differences in stress levels. However, the reported analysis indicated a significant difference by sex. The relationship between occupational stress and teaching performance was weak and statistically non-significant. The findings highlight the importance of manageable workloads, clearly defined responsibilities, professional development, and institutional support in promoting teacher well-being. Further research involving broader populations and additional organizational factors is recommended.

items.abstract: 摘要： 人机协作作为提升企业创新和效率的关键驱动力, 领导在此过程中发挥了核心作用。然而现有研究主要聚焦员工视角, 很大程度上忽视了领导对下属人机协作的多元化认知与行为反应, 因而难以解释领导对人机协作的主观判断为何可能偏离其实际绩效表现。这种认知偏差不仅可能影响领导对人机协作的判断与管理, 也反映出现有研究尚未充分探讨领导多元反应的形成机制及其有效性。鉴于此, 本研究基于双系统加工理论, 开展三项相互关联的研究：(1)探讨领导的“冷”反应模式, 即领导对下属人机协作的动机归因和未来影响感知如何引发其发展与变革导向行为; (2)探讨领导的“热”反应模式, 揭示下属人机协作如何激发领导的相对剥夺感, 并促使领导以报复性无礼行为作为防御性应激反应; (3)从动态视角比较领导不同行为反应对人机协作可持续性的影响, 以优化人机协作效能, 助力企业数智化转型。

items.title: SwarmSafe-Delta: Isolating Message Effects on LLM Agent Safety
items.abstract: When a tool-using LLM agent team violates policy, aggregate outcomes do not reveal whether an upstream message changed the executor's action. We introduce SwarmSafe-Delta, a paired executable protocol that freezes upstream computation, varies real, hidden, and format-matched placebo delivery, and scores a single committed action against deterministic benign and risky policy states under preassigned budgets. Across four models and constructed optional tasks, real delivery at $N=4$ produces 21.4% risky-world violations, versus 5.0% with placebo and 1.0% with hidden delivery (paired differences +16.4 and +20.3 percentage points). Real delivery also improves benign task success, illustrating that suppressing communication sacrifices utility. In a second regime constructed to require an upstream lookup route, real delivery improves safe completion by 74.2 points relative to hidden delivery. These effects quantify message-delivery contrasts under specified information dependencies, not naturally occurring failure rates. Exploratory action-level analyses show that the effect depends strongly on whether the upstream message recommends a prerequisite check or direct execution; model differences also largely track these message compositions. The contribution is a controlled, execution-grounded measurement protocol rather than a general claim that agent communication is harmful or protective.

items.title: Swedish teachers’ perceived professional action competence in sustainability and climate change education
items.abstract: This study aims to explore how in-service school teachers in Sweden perceive their professional action competence (PAC) in Sustainability and Climate Change Education (SCCE). Drawing on data from an exploratory survey involving 202 primary and secondary school teachers in Sweden, the study examines three core dimensions of PAC in SCCE: professional knowledge, self-efficacy, and willingness to teach. Descriptive and frequency analyses were employed to identify teachers’ self-perceptions across these dimensions. The study reveals that teachers generally perceive their professional action competence in SCCE as well-prepared, particularly regarding content knowledge and teaching approaches, and they report high levels of intrinsic motivation for teaching SCCE. However, the results also show several areas across these dimensions in which teachers felt less prepared: (1) to facilitate collective action-taking by students, (2) to engage with community partners beyond school in the teaching and learning process, (3) to support students in dealing with difficult emotions, and (4) to assess students’ sustainability-related competences. The study provides valuable insights into the conditions that support or constrain the implementation of SCCE in schools and aims to inform the design of future professional development initiatives and contribute to ongoing efforts to strengthen teachers’ preparedness for transformative SCCE.
