items.title: Sycophantic AI feedback and disconfirming evidence search among business students
items.abstract: Generative AI may influence learning by shaping which evidence students choose to encounter, even when it does not determine their final answer. This study examines whether sycophantic feedback is associated with reduced search for information opposing an initial business judgement and whether perceived judgement correctness accounts statistically for that relationship. A questionnaire-based decision task conducted in September 2025 yielded 405 retained behavioural records from students at 16 Chinese universities. Participants received one of two assigned feedback conditions and opened four of eight materials concerning a fictional business expansion decision. The sycophantic group allocated 36.7% of its openings to opposing materials, compared with 47.5% in the evidence-based comparison group, an unadjusted difference of − 10.9 percentage points (95% confidence interval − 15.5 to − 6.2). An exploratory conditional choice model that respected the four-of-eight constraint and adjusted for material preferences within initial positions yielded an opposition-related odds multiplier of 0.458 (95% confidence interval 0.326–0.645). In the common 297-participant path-analysis sample, under the principal ordinary-least-squares model, the estimated indirect component through post-feedback correctness was − 0.015 (bootstrap 95% confidence interval − 0.031 to − 0.002). This pathway was sensitive to school clustering and modest hypothetical residual confounding; the auxiliary self-report contrast was not significant. The findings locate a potential cost of affirming AI feedback at the evidence-acquisition stage. They support an account of altered information allocation more strongly than a uniquely identified psychological mechanism or a general decline in critical-thinking ability.

items.title: Technologies for Visualizing Organizational and Educational Information from the Standpoint of Pedagogical Neurodesign
items.abstract: Purpose of the study. The paper provides a theoretical justification and a practical test of technologies for visualizing organizational and educational information that are constructed from the standpoint of pedagogical neurodesign and the services, implemented with generative neural network available to users in Russia. The relevance of the paper follows from the expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence in the preparation of visual materials. Visualization facilitates the perception of educational and organizational material and contributes to the strength of its assimilation; however, visualization remains a labor-intensive process requiring special training form the lecturer in the graphical presentation of information. Generative neural network services reduce this labour intensity and make the preparation of an image available to the teacher without a designer, so the central question becomes what the technologies of visualization should be like for the result to match the didactic task, the regularities of visual perception and the limits of the learner’s working memory. The objectives are to clarify the notion of pedagogical neurodesign and to highlight the parameters of the visual presentation of information, to compare the output formats of visual objects and create a model for choosing a format, as well as to describe the software that reproduces this model. Materials and methods. The theoretical basis includes cognitive load theory, the cognitive theory of multimedia learning, dual coding theory, ergonomic requirements for visual presentation of information, the work of domestic researchers on visualization of educational information and on the use of artificial intelligence in vocational education. The methods applied are theoretical analysis and generalization, a comparative analysis of generative neural network services as of July 2026, pedagogical design and prototyping of the software. The empirical basis is the experience of the Laboratory of pedagogical design and virtual reality of the technopark of universal pedagogical competencies named after M.I. Shilova at Krasnoyarsk State Pedagogical University named after V.P. Astafyev. Results. The subjects of visualization of educational and organizational information are identified, which are presented to the learner together and differ in the didactic purpose of the image. The notion of pedagogical neurodesign is clarified, correlated with the smart approach and separated from the instrumental layer of generative services. Six parameters of visual presentation are identified, namely coloristics, typography, contrast, symmetry and unity of form, free space and pictography, for each of which psychophysiological foundation, a design requirement and the consequence of non- compliance are indicated. Five output formats of visual objects are compared and the conditions of their application are defined. A model of format selection is constructed that comprises five steps, from the identification of the type of information to the verification of the result against five criteria. The smart visualization wizard is described, located in the public domain and implementing the specified model in the form of a step-by-step web application. Examples of the visualization of organizational and educational information obtained using it are presented. Conclusion. The quality of a visual learning aid is determined not by the choice of a neural network service but by compliance with the parameters of visual presentation and by the pedagogical verification of the result. A software tool that reproduces the sequence of steps of pedagogical neurodesign saves the didactic task at the core of the teacher’s work and allows students of pedagogical direction of training to master the techniques of designing visual learning aids through an activity-based approach.

items.abstract: 摘要： 人工智能(AI)正加速嵌入应急决策与处置中的关键环节, 在提升任务效率和表现的同时, 却可能阻碍管理者经验的同步增长。本文提出“人工智能经验阻断效应” (experience-blocking effect, EBE), 指的是AI辅助任务中原始情境接触、判断生成、后果承担与反馈校准、反思转化受到压缩、外移、弱化或浅化的近端过程性多维状态。研究1界定EBE的内涵、识别关键表征并构建测量框架; 研究2将替代式AI使用操作化为人-AI-任务配置, 检验其对EBE及任务绩效的影响; 研究3采用纵向、多轮和高仿真情境, 检验EBE是否通过限制情境线索知觉学习和行动-结果关联学习, 使得个人经验内化不足, 并通过减少成员可供外化的经验素材削弱其团队转化, 使团队经验外化不足。该框架将AI辅助应急管理的评价由即时任务绩效拓展至个体与团队经验沉淀, 为兼顾任务效能和管理者经验性专业能力发展的人智协同模式提供依据。

items.title: The face matching performance of human-algorithm teams over time (EFCT)
items.abstract: We often need to identify someone based on their facial appearance. In applied settings, verification is commonly a one-to-one matching task, in which we compare an individual’s appearance to the photograph on their identification document (such as a driver’s licence or passport). While face matching was once only performed by humans, it is becoming more common for the task to incorporate facial recognition technologies, such as Automated Facial Recognition (AFR) systems. While specific details about how the human and technology operate together are often situationally dependent, here we are interested in a general paradigm in which the algorithm provides the human with a prediction to evaluate (i.e., whether the two images show the “same” person or two “different” people), but the human has full control over the final identification decision made. Unaided by technology, human performance on unfamiliar face matching tasks is often characterised as being “error prone”, with average accuracy of 60-90% common in standardised laboratory tasks (for a review see Fysh & Bindemann, 2017). On high quality imagery, modern facial recognition systems that leverage Deep Convolutional Neural Networks can achieve exceptional levels of accuracy that exceed human performance (Carragher & Hancock, 2020; Grother et al., 2025; White et al., 2015). But our past research has shown that while humans can improve their own face matching performance when using algorithms as decision aids, the average aided performance of the human is significantly worse than the algorithm alone (Carragher & Hancock, 2023). That is, the average human fails to correct algorithm errors, while also overturning correct decisions from the system (see also Carragher et al., 2024; Hua et al., 2025). In our research so far, participants have been novices (either undergraduate students or members of the public), who have completed a laboratory face matching task with assistance from a simulated Automated Facial Recognition (sAFR) system. In Carragher and Hancock (2023), participants completed the Expertise in Facial Comparison Task (EFCT: White et al., 2015), which consists of 168 trials in total. However, with the procedure we had at the time, participants only completed half the trials (84) with assistance from the algorithm. In Carragher et al. (2024), participants completed the short version of the Glasgow Face Matching Test 2 (GFMT2-S: White et al., 2022), which consists of 80 trials total, but again only had assistance from the algorithm on half the trials. In Hua et al. (2025), participants completed 78 trials with algorithm assistance, in a task that combined the short Kent Face Matching Task (KFMT: Fysh & Bindemann, 2018a) and the unfamiliar portion of the Stirling Familiar Face Matching Task (Carragher & Hancock, 2020). In Mueller et al. (2024), participants completed 160 trials with assistance from an algorithm. The longest algorithm assisted face matching task we are aware of was conducted by Fysh and Bindemann (2018b), who had participants complete 210 trials from the Kent University Face Database (Fysh & Bindemann, 2018a) – however, the algorithm in this study was relatively inaccurate, providing the correct response on 60% of trials (for further discussion see Carragher and Hancock, 2023). The face matching tasks in these experiments would all take less than 30 minutes to complete (some of these papers do not report experiment duration, but on average, participants submit face matching decisions in about 5 seconds – see Fysh & Bindemann, 2018a). Human-algorithm teaming for face matching is likely to occur in applied settings where operators are professional staff. In these settings, it is possible that a shift may last longer than 30 minutes. Studies of human face matching ability suggest that performance decreases as the task progresses. Alenezi and Bindemann (2015) had participants complete the same 200 trial face matching task 5 times in a single session, for 1000 trials total (25 blocks of 40 trials). Overall accuracy, and perceptual sensitivity (d’), decreased significantly over the course of the experiment. This effect is consistent with the well-known vigilance decrement that occurs in tasks with long durations (Mackworth, 1948; Warm et al., 1996; Warm et al., 2008). Alenezi and Bindemann (2015) also found a significant shift in response bias over time. As the task progressed, participants became more likely to respond “match” to all trials. To the best of our knowledge, no one has yet investigated whether, and how, the face matching performance of human-algorithm teams changes over time. The overarching aim of the current experiment is to investigate whether the performance of human algorithm teams changes over the course of a “long” face matching task. Because the human will be asked to make the final identification decision, this question is more specifically about how human use of the algorithm’s decision changes over time. Of course, one of the benefits of AFR systems is that they do not suffer from time on task or fatigue effects. Carragher et al. (2024) reported that participants generally held more favourable attitudes toward the sAFR system after using it as a decision aid in a face matching task. On every trial of the current experiment, participants in the main experiment (sAFR condition) will submit two identification decisions – one unaided and one aided by the sAFR system. We expect that their unaided performance will decrease over time, as per Alenezi and Bindemann (2015). But based on Carragher et al. (2024), we expect that participants will show greater reliance on the sAFR system as the experiment progresses. Because the sAFR system will be given a level of accuracy that significantly exceeds the average participant (based on prior human accuracy data), this greater reliance is likely to show as an improvement in assisted accuracy over time. However, because we are expecting greater system reliance, we think it is unlikely the average participant will achieve a level of average assisted performance that exceeds that of the system alone (i.e., a collaborative performance gain) - which has not been seen in our previous work either (Carragher & Hancock, 2023; Carragher et al., 2024; Hua et al., 2025; Mueller et al., 2024). Finally, with this greater reliance, we expect that participants will be less likely to correct system errors as the experiment progresses. In addition to our main experimental condition (sAFR condition), we will also recruit a control condition to do the same long face matching task, but without assistance from a sAFR system at all.

items.title: The influence of AI chatbots’ human-like and technical characteristics on users’ perceived addictiveness
items.abstract: With the widespread adoption of generative AI chatbots, their human-like and technical characteristics may enhance user experience while also increasing the risks of overdependence and potential addiction. However, how these two categories of characteristics jointly shape users’ perceived addictiveness remains insufficiently understood. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework, this study developed a model integrating perceived empathy, social presence, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, trust, emotional attachment, functional dependence, and perceived addictiveness. Data were collected from 345 Chinese AI chatbot users through an online survey and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results showed that perceived empathy, social presence, perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of use all positively influenced trust, which in turn strengthened emotional attachment and functional dependence. Both emotional attachment and functional dependence increased perceived addictiveness, with emotional attachment exerting the stronger effect. Mediation analysis further indicated that chatbot characteristics indirectly influenced perceived addictiveness through two parallel pathways: trust–emotional attachment and trust–functional dependence. These findings reveal the emotional and functional mechanisms underlying perceived AI chatbot addictiveness, extend the S–O–R framework, and provide implications for responsible design, calibrated trust, and dependence-risk governance.

items.title: The social embeddedness of trust in AI: Insights from AI decision aids in renewable energy siting
items.abstract: The rapidly expanding employment of AI decision aids in complex and controversial decision-making processes means that trust in AI is becoming ever more important. While existing research examines a range of human- and AI-related factors affecting trust, contextual influences are often only narrowly conceptualized as task characteristics or organizational settings. This paper argues that understanding trust in AI in contested decision-making contexts requires focusing on how stakeholders assess AI’s trustworthiness in relation to their prior experiences with decision-makers and institutions. We develop a framework that conceptualizes the social structures in which AI decision aids are embedded and examine how these structures shape trust in AI. The framework brings together sociological theories on how trust assessments are shaped by past experiences ( ‘shadow of the past’ ), differentiated accounts of institutional trust , and theories of trust transfer . We analyze the case of an AI-augmented geographic information system (AI-GIS) developed to support spatial planning for onshore wind energy in Germany, a field characterized by regulatory complexity and contestation. By combining qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) with qualitative content analysis, the study identifies four distinct ways in which trust in AI is socially embedded: (1) trust in decision-makers extends to AI-GIS as a tool they employ; (2) mistrust in institutions gives rise to trust in AI-GIS as a means of compensating for institutional shortcomings; (3) generalized distrust in decision-makers and institutions is transferred to AI-GIS as a continuation of existing, distrusted structures; (4) trust in institutions and distrust in decision-makers remain disconnected from mistrust in AI-GIS.

items.title: Twenty-Five-Year Seroprevalence of HIV Infection Among Burn Admissions at a National Burns Referral Centre in Oman: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Register Study, 1999–2024
items.abstract: Introduction Burn injury and HIV infection have important clinical and occupational-health implications. However, burn-unit HIV seroprevalence data have not previously been published from the Arabian Gulf. We aimed to estimate HIV seroprevalence among burn admissions to Oman's national burns referral centre over 25 years and describe patient characteristics and outcomes. Materials and Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional register study of the unit's HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody screening register from October 1999 to December 2024. An admission was classified as reactive if any associated result was reactive; confirmed infection required repeat reactive/positive results during the same admission. The register shifted from qualitative negative/positive reporting, predominantly during 1999–2008, to quantitative signal-to-cutoff reporting, predominantly from 2010; manufacturer-specific assay details were not consistently available. Results Of 2,152 admission episodes, 1,705 (79.2%; 1,703 unique patients) had interpretable HIV results; 447 (20.8%) did not. Median age was 17 years, 61.1% were male, and 48.4% were younger than 15 years. TBSA was documented for 958/1,705 admissions (56.2%; median 19%, IQR 10–39%). Among these 958 admissions, in-hospital mortality increased across TBSA categories from 0.5% (<20%) to 5.4% (20–39%) and 36.2% (≥40%) (Cochran–Armitage trend test, p<0.001; Pearson χ²=235.5, df=2). One admission had confirmed HIV infection, giving a seroprevalence of 0.06% (95% CI 0.001–0.33%). Two additional admissions had unconfirmed reactive screens; including these gives an upper-bound estimate of 0.18% (95% CI 0.04–0.51%). Oman's modelled national prevalence is approximately 0.02% (0.2 per 1,000). Conclusion Confirmed HIV seroprevalence was very low and comparable with Oman's national estimate in this national referral population. Findings support careful interpretation of reactive screens and reflex confirmatory testing. The study was approved by the Khoula Hospital Ethical Board.

items.title: Understanding Clinician Engagement with AI in Radiology: Protocol for a Pre-Implementation Qualitative Study to Inform Learning-to-Defer System Design
items.abstract: This project is a qualitative study of clinical decision-making in chest X-ray (CXR) interpretation at Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (OUH), a setting in which multiple AI tools have recently been evaluated and in which a Learning-to-defer (L2D) system is in development. It constitutes a case study of clinician engagement with AI in radiology. This sits within a broader project examining how cognitive mechanisms and system-level factors shape clinicians' engagement with AI tools across different stages of development, implementation, and use. At the radiology site, this work will inform the design of a prototype L2D system: a human–AI set-up in which the AI either makes a decision itself or routes (defers) it to a human, based on their respective past performance. Component A of this protocol addresses the question of how trust, advice-taking, and group decision-making operate within the CXR reporting pathway, and what sociotechnical conditions shape AI engagement in this setting. It will also explore the system attributes which influence the safe implementation of an L2D tool that is being developed for radiology. Component B of the protocol directly addresses questions related to the design requirements of the L2D system: what deferral format would clinicians accept, who should receive deferred cases, how should deferral decisions be presented, and what outcome criteria would constitute meaningful benefit? These questions require an understanding of the psychological mechanisms that clinicians rely on when engaging with AI tools, and of the clinical system in which clinicians work. Overall, the study aims to build the evidence base that responsible development and deployment of such a system will require. This way, the technical design of the L2D system can be grounded in an understanding of who makes decisions, how, under what conditions, and practically what meaningful benefit would look like in this setting. The analysis draws on theories of trust, advice-taking, and group decision-making, situated within sociotechnical frameworks for understanding healthcare work (Systems Engineering Initiative for Patient Safety [SEIPS] 2.0; nonadoption, abandonment, scale-up, spread, and sustainability [NASSS] framework).

items.title: Understanding data ecosystems: Conceptual foundations of the phenomenon
items.abstract: Abstract Data ecosystems are increasingly recognized as critical to digital supply chains as they enable firms to access, exchange, govern, and mobilize data for coordinated action. These complex sociotechnical networks enable diverse stakeholders to engage in generating, sharing, and processing data, thereby fostering value creation across various industries. Yet despite growing interest, literature still lacks a consolidated understanding of what constitutes a data ecosystem and how its core elements interrelate. To address these issues, the present study employs a multimethod research design comprising a systematic literature review and a case study involving eight data ecosystem actors. The findings identify four constitutive subsystems of the data ecosystem: stakeholders, infrastructure, data, and governance, along with their underlying components. The study identifies six interrelations among these components, showing that data ecosystems depend not only on the presence of core elements but also on the relationships among them. By integrating insights from prior literature with empirical evidence, the study develops a foundation for understanding data ecosystems. The paper contributes to information systems (IS) research by clarifying the sociotechnical structure of data ecosystems and by providing a basis for future theorizing on interorganizational data sharing, governance, and responsive digital supply chains.

items.abstract: Augmented analytics shifts much of the analytical work in business intelligence (BI) to artificial intelligence (AI), leaving non-technical users with one remaining safeguard: verifying AI-generated insights before acting on them.This paper examines whether trust in augmented analytics is associated with less verification and how verification relates to perceived decision quality.Survey data from 350 non-technical BI users in Vietnam were analysed with partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), using a newly developed tenitem verification behaviour scale (VER).The results suggest that trust is negatively associated with verification, and verification is positively associated with perceived decision quality.The indirect association of trust through verification is negative, whereas its direct association remains positive, consistent with competitive mediation.Perceived explainability is associated with higher trust, but its direct association with verification is not significant, and the hypothesized moderating role of AI literacy receives no statistical support.Because the design is crosssectional and self-reported, the paths represent associations rather than causal effects.Automation complacency and objective decision quality were not measured, and the verification scale was supported by initial validation evidence from one sample.The findings motivate linking insights to their source data, second checks for high-value decisions and direct monitoring of verification; the effectiveness of these proposals remains untested.The study develops a survey measure of verification behaviour with initial validation evidence and shows that the positive trust-decision quality association coexists with a negative indirect association through verification.

items.title: Virtual Reality at the Threshold of Transformation: Paradigms, Empirical Benefits, and Systemic Limitations
items.abstract: Over the past two decades, Virtual Reality (VR) has evolved from an entertainment novelty to a fundamental medium for digital transformation in education, clinical medicine, industrial engineering, and public administration.Combining bibliometric mapping with a critical review of the literature, this paper summarizes the current state of the modern immersive ecosystem, examining its main operational domains, empirical benefits, systemic bottlenecks, and development trajectories.Our results indicate that VR significantly enhances procedural learning, diagnostic accuracy, and collaborative workflows through high-fidelity, risk-free simulations.Placing VR within the broader framework of Extended Reality (XR), we analyze its convergence with Artificial Intelligence, distributed cloud-edge topologies, the Internet of Things (IoT), and Digital Twins.Specifically, we assess how delivery architectures such as Virtual Reality as a Service (VRaaS) mitigate traditional hardware constraints, enabling scalable and concurrent deployment, while documenting the contributions of Romanian research groups in this field.Despite clear benefits in terms of cognitive engagement and operational cost efficiency, large-scale institutional adoption faces persistent challenges, including cybersickness, ergonomic limitations, infrastructure expenses, cybersecurity risks, and data privacy governance.Finally, this analysis highlights VR's transition to a ubiquitous digital tool, arguing that its long-term viability depends on responsible algorithmic design, robust edge infrastructures, and cross-platform interoperability.

items.title: When Experience Becomes Metric: Systemic Model of Distress in Intelligent Digital Environments (SMDIDE)
items.abstract: The disruptions generated by AI within production systems alter the human experience at work and outline the emergence of digital distress in contemporary labor environments. The model was developed through a conceptual methodology based on interdisciplinary synthesis, integrating sociotechnical studies, cognitive psychology, labor theory, and critical AI scholarship. As a result, the SM-DIDE model conceptualizes distress as a dynamic process that arises during human-machine interaction, where cognitive and technological overload is processed as cognitive demand through the functional articulation of six interdependent subsystems. The activation, modulation, and feedback among these subsystems explain the variability in the presentation, course, and trajectories of distress. Three subsystems describe the progression from the perception of cognitive and technological demand to the emergence of evolutionary trajectories. This progression is neither linear nor deterministic: it is modulated by the transversal subsystem of involuntary regulation and by the dysfunctional coping subsystem, both of which interact with the direct influence of the structural modulation subsystem to determine the load exerted on the worker during the interaction with AI. The model reframes distress as a process and directs research toward work environments centered on human experience, integrating domains rarely articulated together—cognitive, epistemic, affective, existential, and sociotechnical—and advancing toward a unified theory of digital distress.

items.title: Where Does Accountability Lie in Deployed AI Systems? Using Cognitive Work Analysis to Address the Value-Alignment Problem
items.abstract: Increased use of Artificial Intelligence raises questions around mitigating unintended consequences. Technical perspectives on these questions lead to calls for “Responsible AI,” while regulatory perspectives lead to calls for increased human oversight. Neither perspective fully addresses the core issues surrounding accountability in the sociotechnical systems in which AI operates. Human oversight is a form of supervisory control, in which the role of the human is to monitor AI performance within defined constraints, and this requires consideration of who defines the constraints, where accountability lies when the constraints are exceeded, and how AI performance can be interpreted by human supervisors. For us, constraints correspond to system’s Values and a challenge lies in aligning system operations with these Values. We demonstrate the use of Work Domain Analysis to map purpose-related functions (i.e., activity performed in a sociotechnical system) to Values (weighted according to the functional purpose of the organization).

items.title: Work Environment Factors and Work Efficiency Among Filipino US Registered Nurses in Remote Utilization Management Roles in The United States Healthcare System
items.abstract: Remote Utilization Management has emerged as an alternative nursing role for Filipino United States Registered Nurses, yet evidence concerning their working conditions and efficiency remains limited. This study examined the relationship between work environment factors and work efficiency and developed an evidence-based training program. Methods: A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was used among 158 Filipino USRNs working in remote Utilization Management. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire measuring physical work environment, technological support, workload, organizational support, communication, work-life balance, leadership, productivity, accuracy, timeliness, decision making, and job performance. Frequency, percentage, mean, independent samples t test, analysis of variance, Welch’s analysis, and Pearson correlation were employed. Results: Respondents generally reported high levels of work environment and work efficiency. Physical work environment and technological support were the strongest workplace dimensions, while workload and work-life balance were comparatively lowest. Quality and accuracy emerged as the strongest efficiency dimension, whereas productivity was comparatively lowest. Work environment and efficiency differed significantly according to educational attainment, civil status, nursing experience, and remote Utilization Management experience, but not according to age or sex. All work environment dimensions had very strong positive relationships with productivity, accuracy, timeliness, decision making, and overall performance. Discussion: The findings indicate that favorable physical, technological, organizational, relational, and psychosocial conditions are integral to efficient remote nursing practice. The REMOTE-UM EXCEL Program was proposed to strengthen ergonomics, technology competence, workflow management, communication, evidence based decisions, leadership, psychological safety, and work-life boundaries. Organizations should implement integrated workplace interventions and evaluate their effects through longitudinal and performance-based measures to support sustained quality, employee well-being, and organizational effectiveness.

items.title: Work motivation in a VUCA environment: a theoretical integration of self-determination theory and the job demands-resources model
items.abstract: The article presents a theoretical analysis of employee work motivation in a VUCA environment characterised by volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity, through the lens of Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model. The study aims to substantiate an integrative conceptual model of the relationships between work environment characteristics, motivational regulation, personal resources, and organisational outcomes; the methodology combines a theoretical literature review, conceptual analysis, and cross-theoretical integration of SDT and JD-R. The analysis shows that job resources support autonomous motivation by satisfying basic psychological needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness, whereas chronically high VUCA-related demands frustrate these needs and shift motivation toward controlled regulation or amotivation. The integrative model identifies key elements — VUCA context, job demands and resources, basic psychological needs, quality of motivational regulation, social-psychological resources, proactive job crafting, and organisational outcomes — and establishes links between them; particular attention is paid to uncertainty tolerance as a personal resource that moderates the impact of an unstable environment on motivational states. The scientific novelty lies in the systematic integration of SDT and JD-R for conditions of chronic organisational uncertainty and in establishing a theoretical correspondence between Gerchikov’s motivational typology and the SDT motivational continuum.

items.title: Workplace Violence, Psychosocial Risks and Mental Health Across Healthcare Professional Groups
items.abstract: Healthcare workers are exposed to workplace violence, yet the extent and nature of this exposure may differ considerably across professional groups. Psychosocial working conditions, including high work demands, emotional demands, working-time pressures and employment relations, may shape the conditions in which workplace violence occurs and is experienced. This study investigates psychosocial risks, workplace violence and symptoms of depression, anxiety and stress among nurses, physicians, healthcare assistants and administrative staff, and examines whether workplace violence is statistically associated with the relationship between psychosocial risks and these symptoms. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 289 Portuguese healthcare workers using three validated instruments: the Psychosocial Risk Factors Scale (INSAT_ERPS), the Aggression and Violence at Work Scale and the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (DASS-21). Group differences were tested with Kruskal–Wallis tests, associations with Spearman correlations, and mediation and moderation analyses were performed using SPSS and the PROCESS macro. Results showed that workplace violence affected all professional groups but was more intense among nurses. Psychosocial risk was strongly associated with workplace violence, and this association did not differ across professional groups. However, neither psychosocial risks nor violence were associated with depression, anxiety or stress, and no statistically significant indirect association was observed. These findings highlight the importance of addressing workplace violence as an organizational and occupational health issue rather than a problem confined to specific professions.

items.title: YQX+: Benchmarking Probabilistic Modeling of Piano Performance Expression
items.abstract: A written music score specifies what notes should be played, but much of the musical meaning of a performance comes from how those notes are interpreted: pianists shape timing, dynamics, tempo, and articulation to communicate structure, style, and emotion. Modeling this expressive aspect of music matters for music education, digital performance rendering, and creative AI systems, and is difficult precisely because the same score admits many different but musically valid interpretations.In this paper, we present YQX+, a benchmarking framework for probabilistic modeling of expressive piano performance. YQX+ shifts the focus from demonstrating a single rendering system to comparing how different models capture the expressive variation observed in human performance. To make that comparison possible, it fixes the prediction task, a shared multi-scale contextual feature representation, and a common evaluation protocol, so that model families are trained and compared on equal footing. Given a symbolic score, every model in the suite predicts the same note-level expressive parameters, including beat period, velocity, timing deviation, and articulation ratio, from features that capture local note context, harmonic texture, phrase structure, and score markings. The suite takes the original YQX Gaussian mixture model (GMM) as its reference point and extends it to XGBoost, variational autoencoders, and conditional flow-matching models.To support perceptual evaluation, we also introduce PerformanceMOS, a data-driven estimator of perceived expressive quality and performance skill from symbolic piano performances. Experiments show that larger-capacity XGBoost and \((\beta)\)-VAE models achieve lower timing and articulation errors than prior baselines, including DExter and VirtuosoNet, and obtain the highest predicted mean opinion scores (MOS). These findings establish YQX+ as a systematic benchmark for probabilistic modeling of piano performance expression, with PerformanceMOS providing a scalable proxy for human listening evaluation. The code, trained models, and evaluation scripts are available at \texttt{https://github.com/kkwsts/YQX-Plus}.

items.title: A Connected Architecture for U.S. Corp-to-Corp Staffing: Representation, Rate Traceability, and Workforce Operations
items.abstract: The architecture described here is targeted at the U.S. market for corp-to-corp (C2C) staffing services. Requirements, representation agreements and negotiation of the rates to be paid are frequently spread out over email threads and messaging groups. Approach. A practitioner-informed conceptual design for such recruitment is developed here from the founder’s descriptions of his current workflow, supplemented by a focused narrative discussion of recruitment accountability, explainable AI and human oversight. The design here comprises six stages. Architecture. A candidate signs the right-to-represent (RTR) agreement(s) for that candidate’s submission and the employing organization acknowledges representation of the candidate(s) by the submitting organization(s). Where a subsequent rate change is negotiated with the candidate a new signature from that candidate is required. Unreadable screenshots require human review to evaluate agreement. items.title: A Teacher's Concerns about AI in Primary School: Critical Thinking, Personal Data and the Fear of Cognitive Dependence
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is already part of pupils' everyday lives and of school life. Written from the perspective of a primary school teacher and principal, this perspective paper examines three interrelated concerns of the author herself. These concerns arose from a wish to protect her pupils and led her to study the topic for her own professional development and to help her colleagues make teaching safer and better. They concern developing critical thinking towards AI-generated answers, protecting the personal data of minors, and the fear that excessive assistance from AI will weaken pupils' thinking. Drawing on a narrative, non-systematic review of recent research on cognitive offloading, the European and Greek regulatory framework, and illustrative examples from the author's own teaching practice and lesson scenarios for primary school, it argues that the fear of cognitive dependence is a plausible concern rather than an established finding for primary school pupils. The available evidence, which comes mainly from adolescents and adults, suggests that the form of AI support (whether it replaces the learner's effort or scaffolds it) may be an important factor. AI is regarded throughout as a valuable tool; the risk lies mainly in the way it is used. The classroom examples come from ordinary lessons whose only purpose was to teach pupils to question AI answers and to protect themselves when using AI. They were not planned as research, no research data were collected, and they are offered as the author's practitioner reflections, not as findings. The author's classroom experience illustrates that such activities can be implemented in ordinary primary school lessons, but their effects on pupils' critical thinking have not yet been evaluated. The paper relates the three concerns to long-standing educational principles, in particular Socratic questioning, Dewey's reflective thought and Vygotskian scaffolding. On this basis, it proposes a simple, as yet untested three-step classroom protocol (``think -- ask -- check''), age-appropriate data protection rules, and a role for school leadership, and outlines questions for future research.

items.title: AI-enabled talent analytics and workforce agility in manufacturing SMEs: the mediating role of human-AI collaboration and the moderating role of technostress resilience
items.abstract: Introduction Small and medium-sized enterprises increasingly use AI-enabled talent analytics (AITA) to support workforce planning and adaptive performance, yet the mechanisms linking AITA to workforce agility (WA) remain underexplored. This study examines human-AI collaboration (HAIC) as a mediating mechanism and technostress resilience (TR) as a psychological resource and boundary condition. Methods A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 334 owners, HR managers, and operations/production heads from Pakistani manufacturing SMEs actively using AITA. Exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling, 5,000 bootstrap resamples, and moderation analyses were used to assess the measurement and structural models. Results AITA was positively associated with WA, and HAIC showed a significant indirect association between AITA and WA, consistent with partial statistical mediation. TR was positively associated with WA and significantly strengthened the AITA-WA association. The exploratory TR x HAIC interaction was not statistically significant. Discussion The findings position AITA as a socio-technical work-design resource whose association with agility depends on human interpretation, collaborative routines, and psychological capacity to manage technology-related demands. Because the data are cross-sectional and based on one knowledgeable respondent per firm, the results should be interpreted as manager-perceived associations rather than causal effects.

items.title: Algorithmic Management as a Double-Edged Form of Digital Work Design: Job Demands, Autonomy and Employee Outcomes across 35 European Countries
items.abstract: Computer-based managerial systems are part of the digital infrastructure of work, with potential implications for employee demands and discretion. Drawing on Job Demands-Resources theory, this study examines task allocation, work scheduling and performance monitoring as distinct functions and their parallel indirect associations with engagement and intention to quit through work intensity and autonomy. Weighted least squares mean- and variance-adjusted structural equation models were estimated for 26,504 employees in 35 European countries using the 2024 European Working Conditions Survey. The measures capture reported computer involvement rather than verified artificial intelligence capabilities. Engagement and autonomy were modelled as latent factors, and quit intention as an ordinal outcome. All three practices were positively associated with work intensity. Task allocation was positively associated with autonomy, whereas monitoring was negatively associated with autonomy; scheduling’s negative autonomy association was less robust to contextual fixed effects. Task allocation showed opposing indirect engagement associations through intensity and autonomy, whereas monitoring showed negative associations through both pathways. Intensity-related indirect associations with quit intention were consistently positive, while autonomy-related indirect associations were not statistically significant in the primary or fixed-effects models. Sensitivity analyses supported the main directional patterns, while exploratory country diagnostics indicated incomplete measurement invariance and heterogeneous slopes. The findings inform the evaluation of digital management by distinguishing functions associated with greater demands and greater autonomy from those associated with greater demands and reduced autonomy. The cross-sectional design does not establish causal mediation or uniform cross-country relationships.

items.title: ALGORITMA SEBAGAI REKAN KERJA: TINJAUAN SISTEMATIS TENTANG DINAMIKA TIM MANUSIA-AI DAN ANJLOKNYA KENDALI MANUSIA (LEMBAGA MANUSIA)
items.abstract: Abstrak: Kecerdasan buatan (artificial intelligence/AI) semakin terlibat dalam pekerjaan organisasi, bukan hanya sebagai alat bantu, melainkan juga sebagai rekan tim semiotonom yang berpartisipasi dalam pembagian tugas, koordinasi, dan pengambilan keputusan. Perkembangan ini menimbulkan pertanyaan tentang cara mempertahankan agensi dan kendali manusia ketika pekerjaan dilakukan bersama AI. Penelitian ini bertujuan mensintesis literatur mengenai dinamika tim manusia-AI dengan berfokus pada alokasi tugas dan otomasi, komunikasi dan kepercayaan, serta mekanisme desain yang dapat menjaga agensi manusia. Penelitian menggunakan metode tinjauan pustaka sistematis (systematic literature review/SLR) dengan proses seleksi berorientasi PRISMA.Tinjauan melaporkan 13 studi yang memenuhi kriteria, terbit pada 2023-2026, dengan desain yang beragam, meliputi tinjauan konseptual, tinjauan integratif dan sistematis, eksperimen, metode campuran, analisis teks, serta studi kasus industri. Sintesis naratif disusun dalam tiga tema, yaitu AI sebagai rekan kerja, dinamika tim manusia-AI, serta erosi agensi dan pengawasan manusia. Berdasarkan ringkasan studi ,alokasi tugas dinamis, antarmuka yang transparan dan dapat dijelaskan, kewenangan intervensi manusia, verifikasi aktif, dan model mental bersama berpotensi mendukung kendali manusia. Sebaliknya, otomasi tinggi tanpa keterlibatan manusia yang memadai, pengawasan pasif, dan ketergantungan tanpa evaluasi kritis dapat melemahkan kesadaran situasional, otonomi, dan akuntabilitas. Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa organisasi perlu merancang pekerjaan berbasis AI dengan kepercayaan yang terkalibrasi, tanggung jawab yang jelas, dan peluang intervensi manusia yang bermakna. Keterbatasan draf terkait jumlah hasil penyaringan dan penilaian risiko bias formal perlu diverifikasi sebelum publikasi.

items.title: Assessing learning beyond AI assistance: assisted performance and unaided retention in generative AI-supported learning
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can improve task performance when support is available, yet these gains do not necessarily indicate what learners retain independently. This Mini Review examines three assessment conditions: assisted task performance, immediate testing without AI, and delayed testing without AI. Relevant evidence was identified through searches of the Web of Science Core Collection and supplementary source identification. Across the reviewed experiments, outcomes varied with task demands, instructional design and the skills assessed. Unrestricted AI assistance was associated with weaker subsequent performance in some comparisons, whereas structured AI-supported instruction showed benefits for selected outcomes. None of the twelve selected studies documented all three conditions with verified AI exclusion at both no-AI posttests. Variation in baseline measurement, follow-up intervals and instructional comparators further limits cross-study interpretation. Retrieval attempts, elaboration and feedback use offer plausible explanations, but their roles as mediators remain largely untested. Future studies should document AI availability during learning and testing, specify the constructs assessed, and report learning activities between assessments.

items.abstract: Estudo observacional, transversal, descritivo e analítico, com abordagem quantitativa, destinado a analisar a associação entre riscos ergonômicos, estresse ocupacional e queixas musculoesqueléticas em bombeiros militares vinculados ao Comando Geral do Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Estado do Pará, em Belém, Pará, Brasil. Os riscos ergonômicos serão avaliados por meio do Job Factors Questionnaire; o estresse ocupacional, pela versão brasileira resumida da Job Stress Scale; e as queixas musculoesqueléticas, pelo Questionário Nórdico de Sintomas Osteomusculares. O modelo estatístico principal será um modelo linear generalizado misto logístico (GLMM), com intercepto aleatório por participante e observações correspondentes às regiões anatômicas avaliadas. O Plano de Análise Estatística foi consolidado e congelado internamente em 29 de agosto de 2026, antes do início da coleta de dados. A coleta teve início em 31 de agosto de 2026 e permanece em andamento na data deste registro. Nenhuma análise descritiva ou inferencial dos dados do estudo foi realizada antes do registro público. O registro tem como finalidade documentar prospectivamente, em relação ao acesso aos resultados e à realização das análises, as hipóteses, os desfechos, as exposições, o planejamento amostral, os modelos estatísticos e as análises de sensibilidade previamente estabelecidas. items.title: Can AI Replace Teachers? A Conceptual Analysis of Instructional Capabilities and Limitations
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has renewed debate about whether technology can replace teachers. This conceptual article examines that question by distinguishing the performance of instructional tasks from responsibility for the wider educational role. A theory-informed synthesis of selected research and institutional guidance is used to develop a framework for allocating teaching responsibilities in higher education. Technological pedagogical content knowledge provides the theoretical foundation, while human-centred AI guidance informs the governance perspective. The framework proposes that suitability for delegation depends on task boundedness, evidence of learning, error consequences, learner readiness, and the availability of professional oversight. AI may support explanation, practice, and preliminary feedback, yet success on these tasks does not establish equivalence across assessment judgment, contextual adaptation, relational support, and institutional accountability. Recent experimental research illustrates both the potential of carefully designed AI tutoring and the risk of confusing assisted performance with independent learning. Six conceptual propositions and a task-allocation matrix are presented. The article recommends evaluating AI-supported arrangements against explicit learning and accountability criteria rather than assuming either universal replacement or universal human superiority. No primary data is reported. The contribution is a conditional account of when AI may substitute for instructional activities and when a teacher-led arrangement remains warranted

items.title: Chat-Bloom: A Taxonomy for Classifying Cognitive Offloading in Student-AI Interactions in CS Education
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are transforming computer science (CS) education by providing immediate problem solving support and on-demand knowledge. However, commercial LLMs frequently deliver complete solutions, fostering overreliance and diminishing the productive struggle essential for deep learning. Neurological evidence further suggests that LLM dependence can significantly reduce brain activity, threatening long-term retention. In response, educators have begun customizing LLM-based AI assistants to deliver structured scaffolding. Despite these efforts, the effect of cognitive offloading in student–AI interactions on CS learning outcomes remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose Chat-Bloom (CB), a taxonomy that classifies the cognitive offloading level of both student prompts and AI responses. We validated CB through inter-rater reliability testing (Gwet's AC2 = 0.81) and trained machine learning (ML) models to achieve 81% classification accuracy for large-scale analysis. Applying CB to CS1 chat logs, we identify distinct interaction sequences, compare cognitive offloading patterns across AI assistants, and examine their relationship to student outcomes. These findings position CB as a practical framework for evaluating and improving AI-assisted learning in CS education.
